name: Tell a good two-minute story
blurb: A story with a shape: a situation, a complication, a turn and a point. Having three ready is the difference between contributing to a conversation and just responding to it.
steps: Mine your life for three raw stories: a time something went wrong, a time you were surprised, a time you were wrong about something.
Give each a structure: set the scene fast, raise a problem, build to one clear turn, and land a point without explaining it.
Cut ruthlessly. Names, dates and side details that do not serve the turn should go.
Write the first line and the last line word for word; improvise everything in between.
Rehearse aloud and time it. Two minutes is much shorter than it feels.
Tell each story to five different people and notice where their attention drifts. Cut those bits.
tips: Preamble is where stories die. Start in the middle of the action.
Do not explain the moral. If the story needs it, the story is not finished.
Present tense and dialogue both make a story feel immediate.
proof: You tell a story at a dinner table and the room goes quiet until the end.
